You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC pattern note

## Two-panel occupancy intersection
When an ARC input is two equal-sized panels separated by a uniform divider row/column, and each panel is mostly a distinct nonzero background color with holes represented by 0, compare cells at identical coordinates. Output a panel of the same dimensions, placing color 2 where BOTH input panels are nonzero, and 0 wherever either panel has a hole. Evidence: task-d05f5e8a demos had same-size panels (colors 6/9 and 6/6 with zero holes), and the solved test used this cellwise overlap rule: top 1-panel AND lower 3-panel, output 2 for shared filled positions. Preserve panel orientation and alignment; remove separator from output. Do not output the union or the holes.

## Continual-ARC task-705b0a10: extend the indicated binary-pattern run
The input uses a dominant background (usually 9 or 5) and a secondary pattern color (8, 4, or 0), with large empty-background separators. The output preserves the input and adds color 1 in trailing/background cells to extend a specific patterned row/region; which section is extended varies between demos. Do not recolor or remove the original marks. Empirical evidence: demo 1 added 1s at the right end of the upper pattern, demo 2 added a single 1 at the upper row's far-right edge, demo 3 extended the lower section at its right side with a solid run and alternating placements. Solved test task-705b0a10 (28x29) added only these 1-cells, using 0-based (row,col): (20,28), (22,27), (23,27), (23,28), (25,26), (26,27); all other cells stayed unchanged. This records the verified output signature; derive the extension from each input rather than assuming fixed coordinates or always choosing the same section.
